C_Intl.ToLower.s: Lowercases the characters in a string; casing is locale-dependent and context-sensitive.

C_Intl.ToTitle.s: Titlecases a string using titlecase positions determined by the default Unicode algorithm.
p: The UTF-8 text whose titlecase positions are mapped.
r: The titlecased string, which may be longer or shorter than the original.

C_Intl.ToUpper.s: Uppercases the characters in a string; casing is locale-dependent and context-sensitive.
p: The UTF-8 text whose characters are uppercased.
r: The uppercased string, which may be longer or shorter than the original.

Frame:CreateTitleRegion.s:
Creates a title region on a Frame that allows dragging of the frame with no other code.

Example usage

myFrame.titleRegion = myFrame:CreateTitleRegion() myFrame.titleRegion:SetSize(600, 24) -- 600 wide x 24 tall myFrame.titleRegion:SetPoint("TOPLEFT") -- anchor the titleRegion to top left of myFrame -- this is the drag bar texture myFrame.titleTexture = myFrame:CreateTexture("myFrame_titleTexture", "ARTWORK") myFrame.titleTexture:SetSize(600, 24) -- texture is the same size as the title drag bar myFrame.titleTexture:SetColorTexture( .3, .3 , .3, .5) -- give it a light grey color

note: If the frame is hidden, dragging will not function when it is shown, so implement a function to re-enable dragging when shown

-- -- toggle the frame shown and hidden -- function MyAddOn:Frame_Toggle()

if ( myFrame:IsVisible() ) then --hide the frame if it's visible else --show the frame if it's hidden end end

r: true if the frame propagates keyboard input, false if the frame consumes keyboard input.

Frame:GetRegions.s: Returns a list of non-Frame child regions belonging to the frame.
r: A list of each non-Frame child region (FontString or Texture) belonging to the frame or `nil` if there are noone.

Frame:GetResizeBounds.s: Returns the minimum and maximum size of the frame for user resizing.

Frame:GetRolesetNames.s: Returns the roleset tags assigned to this frame. Returns a list containing 'roleless' if none are assigned.

Frame:GetScale.s: Returns the scale of the frame.

Frame:IsClampedToScreen.s: Returns whether a frame is prevented from being moved off-screen.

Frame:IsEventRegistered.s: Returns whether a frame is registered to an event.
r: True if the frame is registered for an event, false otherwise. Invalid event names always return false.

Frame:IsGamePadButtonEnabled.s: Checks if this frame is configured to receive gamepad button inputs.
r: `true` if this frame is configured to receive gamepad button inputs, `false` if not.

Frame:IsGamePadStickEnabled.s: Checks if this frame is configured to receive gamepad stick inputs.
r: `true` if this frame is configured to receive gamepad stick inputs, `false` if not.

Frame:IsKeyboardEnabled.s: Returns true if keyboard interactivity is enabled for the frame.

Frame:IsMovable.s: Returns true if the frame is movable.
r: True if the frame can be moved using `Frame:StartMoving`, false otherwise.

Frame:IsResizable.s: Returns true if the frame can be resized by the user.

Frame:IsRolesetFiltered.s: Returns whether this frame is hidden because of its rolesets being filtered.

Frame:IsToplevel.s: Returns whether this frame should raise its frame level on mouse interaction.
r: `true` if this is a toplevel frame.

Frame:IsUserPlaced.s: Returns whether the frame has been moved by the user.
r: True if the frame is flagged as user-positioned (either due to `Frame:StartMoving`, `Frame:SetUserPlaced`, or the layout cache), false otherwise.

Frame:LockHighlight.s: Sets the frame or button to always be drawn highlighted.

Frame:Lower.s: Reduces the frame's frame level below all other frames in its strata.

Frame:Raise.s: Increases the frame's frame level above all other frames in its strata

Frame:RegisterAllEvents.s: Flags the frame to receive all events.

Frame:RegisterEvent.s: Registers the frame to an event.
r: Returns true if the frame is successfully registered to the event. Returns false if the frame was already registered to this event. Throws an error if the event is invalid.

Frame:RegisterForDrag.s: Registers the frame for dragging with a mouse button.
p: - A list of mouse buttons to drag with.

Frame:RegisterUnitEvent.s: Registers the frame for a specific event, triggering only for the specified units.
p: A list of units (up to four units).

Frame:RemoveRoleset.s: Removes a roleset tag from this frame.

Frame:ResizeToBoundsRect.s: Addon-safe API for resizing a frame to match the bounds of its children.

Frame:SetAlpha.s: Sets the opacity of the frame.

Frame:SetAlphaGradient.s: Configures a frame to perform an alpha gradient fade on its edges.
p: If 0, defines the gradient for the left and top edges. If 1, the right and bottom edges.
Length of the fade for an edge. Dependent upon the `index` parameter.

Frame:SetAttribute.s: Sets an attribute on the frame.
p: The name of the attribute (case-insensitive) to be modified.

Frame:SetAttributeNoHandler.s: Sets an attribute on the frame without triggering the OnAttributeChanged script.
p: The name of the attribute (case-insensitive) to be modified.

Frame:SetBackdrop.s: Sets the backdrop texture of a frame. Frame:SetBackdrop(nil or { -- defaults bgFile = "bgFile", edgeFile = "edgeFile", tile = false, tileEdge = false, tileSize = 0, edgeSize = 32, insets = { left = 0, right = 0, top = 0, bottom = 0 } })

Frame:SetBackdropColor.s: `Frame`s provide two methods to apply tint to their `Frame:SetBackdrop`: * **SetBackdropColor()** tints the background component of a frame's backdrop * **SetBackdropBorderColor()** tints the border component of a frame's backdrop

Frame:SetClampRectInsets.s: Controls how much of the frame may be moved off-screen.
p: Left clamp region offset. Controls collision with the left edge of the screen, **positive** values allow the frame to be moved off-screen, **negative** values enforce minimum distance to the edge.
Right clamp region offset. Controls collision with the right edge of the screen, **negative** values allow the frame to be moved off-screen, **positive** values enforce minimum distance to the edge.
Top clamp region offset. Controls collision with the top edge of the screen, **negative** values allow the frame to be moved off-screen, **positive** values enforce minimum distance to the edge.

Bottom clamp region offset. Controls collision with the bottom edge of the screen, **positive** values allow the frame to be moved off-screen, **negative** values enforce minimum distance to the edge.

Frame:SetClampedToScreen.s: Prevents the frame from moving off-screen.
p: True to enable clamping, false to permit moving off-screen.

Frame:SetFlattensRenderLayers.s: Controls whether all subregions are composited into a single render layer.
p: If true, enables render layer flattening.

Frame:SetFrameLevel.s: Sets the level at which the frame is layered relative to others in its strata.
p: Layering level of the frame relative to others in its frameStrata.

Frame:SetFrameStrata.s: Sets the layering strata of the frame.

Frame:SetHitRectInsets.s: Sets the insets of the frame's hit rectangle.
p: Pixels to move the frame's left hit edge to the right by.
Pixels to move the frame's right hit edge to the left by.
Pixels to move the frame's top hit edge down by.
Pixels to move the frame's bottom hit edge up by.

Frame:SetHyperlinkPropagateToParent.s: Enables or disables propagating hyperlink events (ex. OnHyperlinkEnter, OnHyperlinkLeave, OnHyperlinkClick) to this frame's parent.

Frame:SetHyperlinksEnabled.s: Allows mouse interaction with hyperlinks on the frame.
p: True if the mouse should be able to interact with hyperlinks.

Frame:SetID.s: Sets a numeric identifier for the frame.

Frame:SetIsFrameBuffer.s: Controls whether or not a frame is rendered to its own framebuffer prior to being composited atop the UI.
p: `true` to enable rendering this frame to a framebuffer, or `false` to disable.

Frame:SetMaxResize.s: Specifies the maximum width and height that the object can be resized to. frame:SetMaxResize(maxWidth,maxHeight);

Frame:SetMinResize.s: Specifies the minimum width and height that the object can be resized to. frame:SetMinResize(minWidth,minHeight);

Frame:SetMovable.s: Sets whether the frame can be moved.
p: true to allow the frame to be moved using `Frame:StartMoving`, false to disallow.

Frame:SetOnUpdateMode.s: Changes when OnUpdate scripts are executed for this object.

Frame:SetPropagateKeyboardInput.s: Sets whether keyboard input is consumed by this frame or propagates to further frames.
p: true to propagate keyboard input further, false to consume keyboard input immediately.

Frame:SetResizable.s: Sets whether the frame can be resized by the user.

Frame:SetResizeBounds.s: Sets the minimum and maximum size of the frame for user resizing.

Frame:SetRolesets.s: Sets the roleset tags for this frame, used by the UI mode system to gate visibility. Supports comma-separated names to assign multiple rolesets. Pass nil to clear.

Frame:SetScale.s: Sets the size scaling of the frame.

Frame:SetToplevel.s: Controls whether or not a frame should raise its frame level on mouse interaction.
p: If true, to marks this frame as a toplevel frame.

Frame:SetUserPlaced.s: Sets whether a frame has been moved by the user and will be saved in the layout cache.
p: True if the frame has been moved by the user.

Frame:StartMoving.s: Begins repositioning the frame via mouse movement.

Frame:StartSizing.s: Begins resizing the frame via mouse movement.
p: Determines the direction that resizing occurs.

Frame:StopMovingOrSizing.s: Stops moving or resizing the frame, and anchors the point that is closest to a UIParent point to that.

Frame:UnlockHighlight.s: Sets the frame or button to not always be drawn highlighted.

Frame:UnregisterAllEvents.s: Unregisters all events from the frame.

Frame:UnregisterEvent.s: Unregisters an event from the frame.
r: Returns true if the event was successfully unregistered, false if already unregistered. Throws an error is the event is invalid.

FrameScriptObject:AddAccessRestrictions.s: Adds access restrictions to a script object, preventing it from being used in API calls when enforced.

FrameScriptObject:AddForbiddenAspects.s: Adds forbidden aspects to a script object, restricting access to various functionalities such as script bindings.

FrameScriptObject:CanBeAccessedInContext.s: Returns whether the current Lua execution context has permission to access this object.
r: False if access is denied, such as when execution is tainted and the object is forbidden or enforcing access restrictions.

FrameScriptObject:GetAccessRestrictions.s: Returns the mask of all access restrictions applied to this object.

FrameScriptObject:GetForbiddenAspects.s: Returns the mask of all forbidden aspects applied to this object.

FrameScriptObject:GetInheritableForbidde.s: Returns the mask of all forbidden aspects applied to this object that can propagate to others.

r: The name of the frame. This is also a variable in the global namespace.

FrameScriptObject:HasAccessConstraints.s: Returns whether this object has any access constraints that may limit access from some Lua execution contexts.
r: True if this object is forbidden or subject to conditional access restrictions.

FrameScriptObject:HasAnyAccessRestrictio.s: Returns true if this object has any of the supplied access restrictions applied.

FrameScriptObject:HasAnyForbiddenAspect.s: Returns true if this object has any of the supplied forbidden aspects added.

FrameScriptObject:HasAnyForbiddenAspects.s: Returns true if this object has any of the supplied forbidden aspects added.

FrameScriptObject:IsForbidden.s: Returns whether this object has been explicitly marked as forbidden.
r: True if this object has been explicitly marked as forbidden, regardless of the current Lua execution context.

FrameScriptObject:IsObjectType.s: Returns true if the widget object belongs to a given widget type or its subtypes.

FrameScriptObject:SetForbidden.s: Sets the object to be forbidden from an insecure execution path.

FrameScriptObject:SetToDefaults.s: Reset all script accessible values to their default values. If possible, clears secret states.

FrameXML:Debug.s: Queries or sets the FrameXML debug logging flag.
p: `0` to disable debug logging, or `1` to enable it. If not specified, the logging flag will not be modified.

GMSurveyQuestion.s: Returns the text of a specific question from a GM survey.

GameTooltip:AddAtlas.s: Adds an atlas texture to the tooltip.

GameTooltip:AddDoubleLine.s: Add a line to a GameTooltip consisting of a left-aligned part and a right-aligned part.

GameTooltip:AddLine.s: Appends a line of text to the tooltip widget.

GameTooltip:AddTexture.s: Adds a texture (icon) to the beginning of the last line added by AddLine(), AddDoubleLine(), etc.

GameTooltip:ClearLines.s: Clear the lines of a tooltip, both left and right. GameTooltip:ClearLines();

GameTooltip:ClearPadding.s: Set all padding values to 0.0 and remove the Padding SecretAspect.

GameTooltip:FadeOut.s:
Initiates fading out of the GameTooltip over the next few seconds.

Note: the game itself does not call this method to fade out the tooltips, although the effect is similar.

GameTooltip:GetItem.s:
itemName, ItemLink = *GameTooltip*:GetItem();

Returns the name and link of the item displayed on a GameTooltip.

GameTooltip:GetOwner.s: Returns the frame to which the tooltip is anchored.

GameTooltip:GetPadding.s: Returns the amount of space between tooltip's text and its edges.

GameTooltip:GetSpell.s: Returns the name and id of the spell displayed on a GameTooltip.

GameTooltip:GetUnit.s: Returns the name and UnitId of the unit displayed on a GameTooltip.

GameTooltip:NumLines.s: Returns the number of text lines in the GameTooltip object.
r: Returns `0` if the tooltip is empty.

GameTooltip:SetAction.s: Shows the tooltip for the specified action button.

GameTooltip:SetAuctionSellItem.s: Sets the GameTooltip to the item that is in the sell frame of the auction window. GameTooltip:SetAuctionSellItem();

GameTooltip:SetBagItem.s:
hasCooldown, repairCost = GameTooltip:SetBagItem(bag, slot);

Sets the GameTooltip to contain text information about the specified item, as well as returning whether the item is "cooling down" and the cost to repair the item (which may be 0 (or nil?) if non-applicable).

GameTooltip:SetCurrencyToken.s: Shows the tooltip for the specified token type.

GameTooltip:SetFrameStack.s: Displays the frame stack of the mouse cursor's current position on the tooltip. This is not intended to be used in typical addons, but is part of the Blizzard_DebugTools "builtin addon" inspired by DevTools.

GameTooltip:SetHyperlink.s: Changes the tooltip to display the linked object.

GameTooltip:SetInboxItem.s: Shows the tooltip for the specified mail inbox item.
p: Integer - The index of the message to get information from.
Integer - The index of the attachment to get information from. In the range of [1,ATTACHMENTS_MAX_RECEIVE(16)]

GameTooltip:SetInventoryItem.s:
hasItem, hasCooldown, repairCost = Tooltip:SetInventoryItem("unit", invSlot {, nameOnly, hideUselessStats});

This function sets a tooltip widget to display information for the given unit's given inventory slot.

GameTooltip:SetItemKey.s: Shows an ItemKey in a tooltip.

GameTooltip:SetLootItem.s: Sets the GameTooltip to show a loot item.

GameTooltip:SetOwner.s: Anchors the tooltip to a temporary owner. GameTooltip:SetOwner(owner, "anchor"[, ofsX, ofsY]);

GameTooltip:SetPadding.s: Resizes the GameTooltip border and background around its content.

GameTooltip:SetPlayerBuff.s: Sets a GameTooltip to a player buff of the type last used in GetPlayerBuff.

GameTooltip:SetReforgeItem.s: Shows the tooltip for the item being reforged.

GameTooltip:SetSpellBookItem.s: Shows the tooltip for the specified spell. GameTooltip:SetSpellBookItem(spellBookId, bookType);
p: `number` - the id of the spell on the tab from the spellbook - not the same as SpellId

GameTooltip:SetTalent.s: Shows the tooltip for the specified talent.

GameTooltip:SetText.s: Sets the text of a tooltip.

GameTooltip:SetTransmogrifyItem.s: Shows the tooltip when there is a pending (de)transmogrification

GameTooltip:SetUnit.s: Makes a GameTooltip widget display information about a unit.

GameTooltip:SetUnitAura.s: **GameTooltip:SetUnitAura** shows the tooltip for a unit's aura.

GameTooltip:SetUnitBuff.s: Shows the tooltip for a unit's buff.

GameTooltip:SetUnitConsolidatedBuff.s: Shows a tooltip for the spell currently providing the specified consolidated buff type. Displays the tooltip of the spell providing a consolidated buff effect.

GameTooltip:SetUnitDebuff.s: Shows the tooltip for a unit's debuff.

GameTooltip:SetUpgradeItem.s:
Sets the tooltip for the item being upgraded. https://github.com/Ketho/wow-ui-source/blob/d5ae1cda8a81465a775130f7a3c76b2f5ce5cc79/AddOns/Blizzard_ItemUpgradeUI/Blizzard_ItemUpgradeUI.xml#L285

The GameTooltip is shown and set when hovering over [https://github.com/Ketho/wow-ui-source/blob/d5ae1cda8a81465a775130f7a3c76b2f5ce5cc79/AddOns/Blizzard_ItemUpgradeUI/Blizzard_ItemUpgradeUI.xml#L201-306 ItemUpgradeFrame.ItemButton]

GetAbandonQuestName.s: Returns the name of a quest that will be abandoned if `AbandonQuest` is called.
r: Name of the quest that will be abandoned.

GetAccountExpansionLevel.s: Returns the expansion level the account has been flagged for.
r: The expansion the player's game license has been flagged for.

GetAchievementCategory.s: Returns the category number the requested achievement belongs to.
p: ID of the achievement to retrieve information for.

GetAchievementComparisonInfo.s: Returns information about the comparison unit's achievements.
p: ID of the achievement to retrieve information for.
r: Returns true/false depending on whether the unit has completed the achievement or not.
Month in which the unit has completed the achievement. Returns nil if completed is false.
Day of the month in which the unit has completed the achievement. Returns nil if completed is false.
Year (two digits, 21st century is assumed) in which the unit has completed the achievement. Returns nil if completed is false.

GetAchievementCriteriaInfo.s: Returns info for the specified achievement criteria.
p: Achievement ID the queried criteria belongs to.
Index of the criteria to query, ascending from 1 up to GetAchievementNumCriteria(achievementID).
Unique ID of the criteria to query.
r: Criteria type; specifies the meaning of the assetID.
True if you've completed this criteria; false otherwise.
The required quantity for the criteria. Used mostly in achievements with progress bars. Usually 0.
The name of the character that completed this achievement.
Criteria data whose meaning depends on the type.
The string used to display the current quantity. Usually the string form of the quantity return.
True if the criteria is eligible to be completed; false otherwise. Used to determine whether to show the criteria line in the objectives tracker in red or not.

p: ID of the achievement to retrieve information for.
An offset into the achievement category, between 1 and `GetCategoryNumAchievements`(categoryID)
r: Points awarded for completing this achievement.
Returns true/false depending if you've completed this achievement on any character.
Month this was completed. Returns nil if Completed is false.
Day this was completed. Returns nil if Completed is false.
Year this was completed. Returns nil if Completed is false. Returns number of years since 2000.
A bitfield that indicates achievement properties:
The fileID of the icon used for this achievement
Text describing the reward you get for completing this achievement.
Returns true/false depending if this is a guild achievement.
Returns true/false depending if you've completed this achievement on this character.
Your character name if you've completed this achievement, or the name of the first character to complete this achievement.
Returns true/false depending if this is a statistic.

GetAchievementInfoFromCriteria.s: Returns the following fields for the specified Criteria.

GetAchievementNumCriteria.s: Returns the number of criteria for an achievement.
r: The number of criteria required for the given Achievement

GetActionBarPage.s: Returns the current action bar page.
r: integer index of the current action bar page, ascending from 1.

GetActionBarToggles.s: Returns the enabled states for the extra action bars.
r: True if the left-hand bottom action bar is shown, false otherwise.
True if the right-hand bottom action bar is shown, false otherwise.
True if the first (outer) right side action bar is shown, false otherwise.
True if the second (inner) right side action bar is shown, false otherwise.

GetActionCharges.s: Returns information about the charges of a charge-accumulating player ability.
p: The action slot to retrieve data from.
r: The number of charges of the ability currently available.
The maximum number of charges the ability may have available.
Time (per `GetTime`) at which the next charge cooldown began, or `2^32 / 1000` if the spell is not currently recharging.
Time (in seconds) required to gain a charge.
The rate at which the charge cooldown widget's animation should be updated.

GetActionCooldown.s: Returns cooldown info for the specified action slot.
p: The action slot to retrieve data from.
r: The time at which the current cooldown period began (relative to the result of GetTime), or 0 if the cooldown is not active or not applicable.
The duration of the current cooldown period in seconds, or 0 if the cooldown is not active or not applicable.

Indicate if cooldown is enabled, is greater than 0 if a cooldown *could be* active, and 0 if a cooldown cannot be active. This lets you know when a shapeshifting form has ended and the actual countdown has started.
The rate at which the cooldown widget's animation should be updated.

GetActionCount.s: Returns the available number of uses for an action.
r: How often an item-based action (see details) may be performed; or always zero for other action types.

p: Action slot to retrieve information about.
r: Type of action button. (e.g. spell, item, macro, companion, equipmentset, flyout)
Appropriate identifier for the action specified by actionType -- e.g. spell IDs for spells, item IDs for items, equipment set names for equipment sets.
Additional identifier for the action specified by actionType -- e.g. whether the companion ID is for a MOUNT or a CRITTER companion.

GetActionLossOfControlCooldown.s: Returns information about a loss-of-control cooldown affecting an action.
p: action slot to query information about.
r: time at which the cooldown began, per `GetTime`.
duration of the cooldown in seconds; 0 if the action is not currently affected by a loss-of-control cooldown.

GetActionSelfCastKey.s: Gets the key that activates self-casting.

GetActionText.s: Returns the label text for an action.

GetActionTexture.s: Returns the icon texture for an action.
r: Returns nil if the slot is empty.

GetActiveArtifactByRace.s: Returns the active Archaeology artifact for a race.
p: Index of the race to pick the artifact from.
r: The description displayed on the artifact detail page. Only visible after completion for rare artifacts.
The rarity of the artifact, 0 for Common and 1 for Rare.
The path to the artifact's icon texture.

The description shown in the tooltip when hovering over the completed artifact. Not visible before the artifact is completed. Not readily available on function call, see SpellMixin:ContinueOnSpellLoad.
The number of Keystone slots this artifact has. Only visible when this is the in progress artifact.
The path to the artifact's background texture. Only displayed when the artifact is rare.

GetActiveSpecGroup.s: Returns the index of the current active specialization/talent/glyph group.
p: (Defaults to false) - If true returns the information for the inspected unit instead of the player.
r: The index of the player's active specialization/talent/glyph group (1 for primary / 2 for secondary).

GetActiveTalentGroup.s: Returns the index of the current active talent group.

GetAddOnCPUUsage.s: Returns the total time used for an addon.
p: The name of the addon to be queried, or an index from 1 to `GetNumAddOns`. The state of Blizzard addons can only be queried by name.
r: The total time used by the specified AddOn, in milliseconds.

GetAddOnDependencies.s: Returns the TOC dependencies of an addon.
p: The name of the addon to be queried, or an index from 1 to `GetNumAddOns`. The state of Blizzard addons can only be queried by name.
r: List of addon names that are a required dependency.

GetAddOnEnableState.s: Get the enabled state of an addon for a character
p: The name of the character to check against or nil.
The name of the addon to be queried, or an index from 1 to `GetNumAddOns`. The state of Blizzard addons can only be queried by name.
r: The enabled state of the addon.

p: The name of the addon to be queried, or an index from 1 to `GetNumAddOns`. The state of Blizzard addons can only be queried by name.
r: The name of the AddOn (the folder name).
The title of the AddOn as listed in the .toc file (presumably this is the appropriate localized one).
The notes about the AddOn from its .toc file (presumably this is the appropriate localized one).
Indicates if the AddOn is loaded or eligible to be loaded, true if it is, false if it is not.

The reason why the AddOn cannot be loaded. This is nil if the addon is loadable, otherwise it contains a string token indicating the reason that can be localized by prepending "ADDON_". ("BANNED", "CORRUPT", "DEMAND_LOADED", "DISABLED", "INCOMPATIBLE", "INTERFACE_VERSION", "MISSING")
Indicates the security status of the AddOn. This is currently "INSECURE" for all user provided addons, "SECURE_PROTECTED" for guarded Blizzard addons, and "SECURE" for all other Blizzard AddOns.

GetAddOnMemoryUsage.s: Returns the memory used for an addon.
p: The name of the addon to be queried, or an index from 1 to `GetNumAddOns`. The state of Blizzard addons can only be queried by name.
r: Memory usage of the addon in kilobytes.

GetAddOnMetadata.s: Returns the TOC metadata of an addon.
p: The index in the addon list. Note that you cannot query Blizzard addons by index.
The name of the addon, case insensitive.
Field name, case insensitive. May be Title, Notes, Author, Version, or anything starting with X-

GetAllowLowLevelRaid.s: Returns whether joining low-level raids is enabled for the current character.

GetArchaeologyInfo.s: Returns the localized name for the Archaeology profession.
r: Localized name of the Archaeology secondary skill

GetArchaeologyRaceInfo.s: Returns the information for a specific race used in Archaeology.
p: Index of the race to query, between 1 and `GetNumArchaeologyRaces`().
r: (fileID) - The texture used by this race in the Archaeology UI.
Item ID of the Keystone used for the race's archaeology projects. Will be *nil* for Fossil as no such item exists.
Number of collected fragments for this race.
Number of fragments required to solve the current artifact
Maximum number of fragments that can be carried

GetArchaeologyRaceInfoByID.s: Returns info for an Archaeology race.
p: ID of the research branch (race) to query from . The following are the valid IDs:
r: (fileID) - The texture used by this race in the Archaeology UI.
The itemID of the Keystone the race uses. Will be nil for Fossil because no such item exists.
Number of collected fragments for this race.
Number of fragments required to solve the current artifact
Maximum number of fragments that can be carried

GetAreaSpiritHealerTime.s: Returns the time left in seconds until the next Spirit Healer resurrection in battlegrounds.
p: Seconds until the Spirit Guide casts its next Area Resurrection. Returns 0 if player is not dead.

GetArenaCurrency.s: Gets the amount of spendable arena points the player has
p: Integer - Amount of arena points that the player has available and can spend

p: Index of the team you want information on, can be a value between 1 and 3.
r: Teams name, nil if they aren't on a team or the data wasn't received yet.
Teams rating, for a team that hasn't played any games this season it'll be 1500
Total games the team has played for the current week
Total games the team has won for the current week

Total games that the team has played this season

Total games that the player has played this season

Float - Amount of green in the teams emblem color
Float - Amount of blue in the teams emblem color
Float - Amount of red in the teams border color
Float - Amount of green in the teams border color
Float - Amount of blue in the teams border color

GetArenaTeamIndexBySize.s: Returns the index of an arena team for the specified team size.
p: team size (number of people), i.e. 2, 3, or 5.
r: arena team index for the specified team size, or nil if the player is not in a team of the specified size.

GetArenaTeamRosterInfo.s: Requests information regarding the arena team that the player is in, see Returns for a full list of what this returns.
p: Index of the team you want information on, can be a value between 1 and 3.
Index of the team member. Starts at 1.
r: 0 denotes team captain, while 1 denotes a regular member.
The localized class of the player.
1 denotes the player being online. nil denotes the player as offline.
Number of games this player has played this week.

Number of games played the entire season.
Number of games this player has won this week.
Players personal rating with this team

GetArmorPenetration.s: Returns the percentage of target's armory your physical attacks ignore due to armor penetration.
r: Percent of armor ignored by your physical attacks.

GetArtifactInfoByRace.s: Returns the information for a specific race's artifact.
p: Index of the race to pick the artifact from.
r: The description displayed on the artifact detail page. Only visible after completion for rare artifacts.
The rarity of the artifact, 0 for Common and 1 for Rare.
The path to the artifact's icon texture.

The description shown in the tooltip when hovering over the completed artifact. Not visible before the artifact is completed. Not readily available on function call, see SpellMixin:ContinueOnSpellLoad.

The path to the artifact's background texture. Only displayed when the artifact is rare.

GetArtifactProgress.s: Returns progress info for the selected Archaeology artifact.
r: Number of collected fragments for selected artifact.
Number of fragments currently added through keystones for selected artifact.
Number of fragments required to solve the selected artifact.

GetAttackPowerForStat.s: Returns the amount of attack power contributed by a specific amount of a stat.
p: Index of the stat (Strength, Agility, ...) to check the bonus AP of.
Amount of the stat to check the AP value of.
r: Amount of attack power granted by the specified amount of the specified stat.

GetAuctionItemBattlePetInfo.s: Retrieves info about one Battle Pet in the current retrieved list of Battle Pets from the Auction House.
p: The index of the item in the list to retrieve info from (normally 1-50, inclusive).

HousingCatalogSearcher:GetAllSearchItems.s: Returns all catalog entries being searched (note these are NOT search results, this is the source collection of what's being searched)

HousingCatalogSearcher:GetNumSearchItems.s: Returns the total number of entries being searched through

HousingCatalogSearcher:GetSearchCount.s: Returns the total number of owned instances across all most recent search result entries

HousingCatalogSearcher:RunSearch.s: Run search with all current param values

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetAllInFilterTag.s: Set the toggle state of all filter tags within a specific group; If active, only entries that match Any of the tags in the group will be included in search results

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetAllowedIndoors.s: Search parameter; If true, entries that can be placed in house interiors will be included in the search; Note many decor objects can be placed both indoors and outdoors, so having only this toggled on may still include decor that can also be placed outdoors

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetAllowedOutdoor.s: Search parameter; If true, entries that can be placed outside in plots will be included in the search; Note many decor objects can be placed both indoors and outdoors, so having only this toggled on may still include decor that can also be placed indoors

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetAutoUpdateOnPa.s: If true, searcher automatically updates results whenever search param values are changed

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetBaseVariantOnl.s: Search parameter; If true, only the base variant of each decor entry will be included

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetCollected.s: Search parameter; If true, includes all owned entries, including those that are in storage OR placed in an owned house or plot; See IsOwnedOnlyActive for a more exclusive toggle

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetCustomizableOn.s: Search parameter; If true, catalog entries that cannot be customized (ie dyed) will be excluded from the search

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetDistinctPerRec.s: Search parameter; If true, only the first entry per recordID will be included

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetEditorModeCont.s: Search parameter; If set, limits search results to only entries that are used/valid in the specified editor mode

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetFilterTagStatu.s: Set the toggle state of a single filter tag within a specific group

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetFilteredCatego.s: Search parameter; If set, limits search results to only those within the specified category

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetFilteredSubcat.s: Search parameter; If set, limits search results to only those within the specified subcategory

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetFirstAcquisiti.s: Search parameter; If true, excludes any entries that do not reward house xp when acquired for the first time

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetOwnedOnly.s: Search parameter; If true, only entries that you own, and have instances of available in storage, will be included; This does not include entries that you own but have all been placed in a house; See IsCollectedActive for param that includes placed entries

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetSearchText.s: Search parameter; If set, multiple text fields are checked for instances of the text, including name, category, subcategory, and data tags
p: Supports advanced search tokens (`'"'` `'-'` and `'|'`), case and accent insensitive; Set nil to clear out the search text

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetStoredOnly.s: Search parameter; If true, only entries that you have instances of available in storage will be included; This does not include entries that you own but have all been placed in a house; See IsCollectedActive for param that includes placed entries

HousingCatalogSearcher:SetUncollected.s: Search parameter; If true, includes entries that are not owned, meaning not available in storage nor placed in any owned houses or plots

StartAuction.s:
<!--desc-->Starts the auction you have created in the Create Auction panel.

The item is that which has been put into the AuctionSellItemButton. That's the slot in the 'create auction' panel.

The minBid and buyoutPrice are in copper. However I cant figure out how to go below 1 silver. So putting in '50' or '10' or '1' will always make the auction do '1 silver'. But '102' will make it do '1 silver 2 copper'.

runTime may be one of the following: 1, 2, 3 for 12, 24, and 48 hours.

Examples:

StartAuction(1,1,1) - Start at 1 silver, buyout 1 silver, time 12 hours StartAuction(1,10,1) - Start at 1 silver, buyout 1 silver, time 12 hours StartAuction(1,100,1) - Start at 1 silver, buyout 1 silver, time 12 hours StartAuction(1,1000,1) - Start at 1 silver, buyout 10 silver, time 12 hours StartAuction(1,10000,2) - Start at 1 silver, buyout 1 gold, time 24 hours StartAuction(101,150,3) - Start at 1 silver 1 copper, buyout at 1 silver 50 copper, time 48 hours

Play with it yourself:

*Go to auction house *Right click on auctioneer *Click on the 'auction' tab *Drag an item to the slot in the 'Create Auction' panel *Type the following into chat window:

/script StartAuction(1,150,1)

*This should create an auction starting at 1 silver, buyout at 1 silver 50 copper, with auction time of 12 hours. *It should say 'Auction Created' in the chat window. *Now if you go to browse the auctions, your items should show up.

date.s:
date() is a reference to the os.date function. It is put in the global table as the os module is not available.

It returns a string or a table containing the user's machine's current date and time (or the time represented by `time`), formatted according to the given string `format`. If one wishes to supply your own format string, then it uses the same rules as strftime() (Windows Mac). The special string `*t` tells the `date()` function to return a table.

This is a mirror of the Lua function os.date().

Note that the default format returned when calling the date() function with no parameters will be different depending on whether the game is running on a Windows or a Macintosh computer. If you want your addon to be compatible with both systems, you should therefore not use date() without parameters, instead, use

to display the date in the default Windows format

-or-

to display the date in the default Macintosh format.

Be aware that if you use an incorrect format string, including any format specifiers not supported by the C library used in WoW, you will get the error message, "format too long". The error has nothing necessarily to do with the length of the format string; it is simply imprecise error wording in that version of Lua.

next.s:
Returns the next key/value pair for a given table and key.

Allows a program to traverse all fields of a table. Its first argument is a table and its second argument is an index in this table. **`next`** returns the next index of the table and the value associated with the index. When called with nil as its second argument, **`next`** returns the first index of the table and its associated value. When called with the last index, or with nil in an empty table, **`next`** returns nil. If the second argument is absent, then it is interpreted as nil.

Lua has no declaration of fields; There is no difference between a field not present in a table or a field with value nil. Therefore, **`next`** only considers fields with non-nil values. The order in which the indices are enumerated is not specified, even for numeric indices. (To traverse a table in numeric order, use a numerical for or the **`ipairs`** function.)

The behavior of **`next`** is undefined if, during the traversal, you assign any value to a non-existent field in the table. Changing values of existing keys or removing keys is alright though.

(if failed) / Variable - If an error occured, error text is returned; if not, ret1 is the first return value of the original function.

table.foreach.s:
Apply the function f to the elements of the table passed. On each iteration the function f is passed the key-value pair of that element in the table. table.foreach(tab, func); foreach(tab, func);

From TableLibraryTutorial of lua-users.org.

> table.foreach({1,"two",3}, print) -- print the key-value pairs 1 1 2 two 3 3 > table.foreach({1,"two",3,"four"}, function(k,v) print(string.rep(v,k)) end) 1 twotwo 333 fourfourfourfour

If the function f returns a non-nil value the iteration loop terminates.

> table.foreach({1,"two",3}, function(k,v) print(k,v) return k<2 and nil end) 1 1 2 two

Tables can contain mixed key-value and index-value elements. table.foreach() will display all of the elements in a table. To only display the index-value elements see table.foreachi(). For more information about this subject see the TablesTutorial.

> t = { 1,2,"three"; pi=3.14159, banana="yellow" } > table.foreach(t, print) 1 1 2 2 3 three pi 3.14159 banana yellow

table.foreachi.s:
From TableLibraryTutorial of lua-users.org.

Apply the function f to the elements of the table passed. On each iteration the function f is passed the index-value pair of that element in the table. This is similar to table.foreach() except that index-value pairs are passed, not key-value pairs. If the function f returns a non-nil value the iteration loop terminates.

> t = { 1,2,"three"; pi=3.14159, banana="yellow" } > table.foreachi(t, print) 1 1 2 2 3 three

Note in the example only the indexed elements of the table are displayed. See the TablesTutorial for more information on key-value and index-value pairs.

Also note that foreachi starts at index [1], increments the index by one repeatedly, and stops running as soon as it reaches a nil value. This is an example:

> t = { [0] = "zero", --will not be counted [1] = "one", --will be counted; 1 [2] = "two", --will be counted; 2 [3] = "three", --will be counted; 3 ["four"] = "four", --will not be counted; returns 3 [5] = "five" } --will never be reached > foreachi(t, print) 1 one 2 two 3 three

In the above, it starts at t[1] (*not* t[0]) and counts to t[3], printing the corresponding values along the way. It then checks t[4], sees it is nil, and stops running. t[5] is never checked - this *will not hit every array index in a table, only the consecutive ones from one up until it hits its first blank index.*

table.freeze.s: Marks a supplied table as frozen, preventing any modifications to its contents, or replacement of its metatable. If the table has a pre-existing metatable with a '__newindex' table or function, assignments will pass through without raising errors. For tainted code, only tables created by the same addon making this function call are permitted to be frozen.

table.getcountinfo.s: Returns detailed information about the number and distribution of entries in the table.
r: The total number of entries in the table.
The number of entries with positive integral keys.

table.getn.s:
<!-- -->

This is used to determine the size of a table. The size of a table is discussed at the top of this page.

> = table.getn({1,2,3}) -- Lua will count the elements if no size is specified 3 > = table.getn({1,2,3; n=10}) -- note, n overrides counting the elements 10 > t = {1,2,3} > table.setn(t, 10) -- set our own size with setn() > = table.getn(t) 10 > = table.getn({1,2,3,nil,5,6}) -- sequence ends at element 3 due to nil value at 4 3

Note that Lua 5.1 has switched to the # operator. #t is the replacement for table.getn(t)

> print( #{1,2,3} ) 3 However, it does not always behave as one might expect. Consider the following sequence: > t = { 1, 2, 3 } > dump (#t) 3

> t[1] = nil > dump (#t) 3

> dump (t) { [2] = 2 [3] = 3 } -- table: 0x807ff70

> dump (#{ [2] = 2, [3] = 3 }) 0 As you can see, the # operator is unpredictable in that it can return different values for tables with identical contents. The Lua 5.1 reference manual has this to say about it http://www.lua.org/manual/5.1/: The length of a table t is defined to be any integer index such that t[n] is not nil and t[n+1] is nil. In other words, be careful with this operator if you are using tables with holes in them. If your table has all its values between [1] and [n] for some n, with no nils in that range, the # operator will return n. Otherwise its result may be unclear.

Note: The reason the returned values are different is because the tables are different. For indexed tables, or tables that start with index values like 1,2,3 for keys, use tinsert and tremove to change the contents. What # returns is actually correct, setting the index value to nil does not change the size of the table for index keys, tremove would.

table.indexof.s: Returns the first integer index whose value compares equal to the specified value, searching consecutively from index 1 until the first nil value.
p: The value for which to search.
r: The first matching index, or nil if no match is found.

table.insert.s:
From TableLibraryTutorial of lua-users.org.

Insert a given value into a table. If a position is given insert the value before the element currently at that position:

> t = { 1,3,"four" } > table.insert(t, 2, "two") -- insert "two" at position before element 2 > = table.concat(t, ", ") 1, two, 3, four

If no position is specified we append the value to the end of the table:

> table.insert(t, 5) -- no position given so append to end > = table.concat(t, ", ") 1, two, 3, four, 5

When a table has an element inserted both the size of the table and the element indices are updated:

> t = { 1,"two",3 } -- create a table > = table.getn(t) -- find current size 3 > table.foreach(t, print) -- display the table contents 1 1 2 two 3 3 > table.insert(t, 1, "inserted") -- insert an element at the start > = table.concat(t, ", ") -- see what we have inserted, 1, two, 3 > = table.getn(t) -- find the size 4 > table.foreach(t, print) -- the indexes have been updated 1 inserted 2 1 3 two 4 3

When no position is specified the element is inserted at the end of the table according to the calculated size. The size of a table may be user specified and not reflect the number of elements, e.g.,

> t = { 1,"two",3; n=10 } -- create a table with user size > table.insert(t, "end") -- insert with no position inserts at "end" > table.foreach(t, print) -- display the table contents 1 1 2 two 3 3 11 end n 11

table.isempty.s: Returns true if the table contains no entries.
r: True if the table contains no entries; otherwise false.

table.isfrozen.s: Returns true if a table has been marked as frozen.

table.keys.s: Returns an array containing the keys of the specified table.
p: The table whose keys will be returned.
r: An array containing the table's keys. The order of the returned keys is unspecified.

table.remove.s:
*Reference: TableLibraryTutorial, Reference Manual*

Remove an element from a table. If a position is specified the element at that position is removed. The remaining elements are reindexed sequentially and the size of the table is updated to reflect the change. The element removed is returned by this function. E.g.,

> t = { 1,"two",3,"four" } -- create a table > = table.getn(t) -- find the size 4 > table.foreach(t, print) -- have a look at the elements 1 1 2 two 3 3 4 four > = table.remove(t,2) -- remove element number 2 and display it two > table.foreach(t, print) -- display the updated table contents 1 1 2 3 3 four > = table.getn(t) -- find the size 3

If no position is given remove the last element in the table which is specified by the size of the table. E.g.,

> t = { 1,"two","three" } > = table.getn(t) -- find the table size (which is removed) 3 > table.foreach(t, print) -- display contents 1 1 2 two 3 three > = table.remove(t) -- remove the element at position "n" three > table.foreach(t, print) -- display updated contents 1 1 2 two > = table.getn(t) -- display new size 2

If the size of the table does not reflect the number of elements nothing is removed, e.g.,

> t = {1,2,3} > table.setn(t,10) -- set user size > table.foreach(t, print) -- display table contents, note size "n" is stored internally 1 1 2 2 3 3 > = table.getn(t) -- find the size 10 > = table.remove(t) -- remove last element nil > = table.getn(t) -- find the updated size 9 > table.foreach(t, print) -- display elements 1 1 2 2 3 3

type.s: This function returns the type of variable was passed to it. t = type(arg1);
p: Any - Value to query the type of.
r: String representation of the argument's type passed: "nil", "number", "string", "boolean", "table", "function", "thread", or "userdata".

unpack.s: Returns values stored in a table's array portion. ... = unpack(t [, first [, last]])
p: A table to unpack values from.
Index of the first value to return (default: 1).
Index of the last value to return (default: `#t`).
r: Mixed - Values contained at indices `first` through `last` in the table.

xpcall.s: Executes a function in protected mode with a custom error handler. success, res1, ... = xpcall(f, msgh [, arg1, ...])
p: The function that will be called.
Error handler function to be used should f cause an error.
r: True if the function succeeded without errors.
